newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weak on U.S. stock and bond mkts.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weak on U.S. stock and bond mkts.

text.p: The Mexican peso moderately extended earlier weakness at the close on Wednesday on what dealers said was demand for dollars prompted by late weakness on the U.S. stock and bond markets.

"Some banks went short (dollars) yesterday, and we saw domestic and foreign big players pick up dollars at the close," a trader said. "Dealers obviously don't feel comfortable staying short right now."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed trade 1.5 centavos weaker at 7.9480/7.9510 and 7.9440/7.9490 per dollar, respectively.
"Dealers closely watched U.S. stock and bond markets, as well as peso futures trading in Chicago MEX02, where we saw some selling," the trader added.
Shortly after the close of foreign exchange trade in Mexico, the Dow Jones was down 102.23 points to 7,655.83, while the U.S. 30-year long bond was off 19/32 to yield 6.74 percent.
Some dealers said dollars were also in demand due to unease ahead of mid-term elections to be held on July 6.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 0.4 of a centavo weaker at 7.9375/7.9420 per dollar.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 7.9400/7.9600 per dollar on Thursday for the 48-hour peso contract.
